formation.explanation: A serialized RawNode.Propose (or node.run proposal event) enters raft.Step. A follower forwards to a known leader or drops; a candidate drops. A leader rejects transfer/removal/quota cases, assigns term/index, appends locally and broadcasts predecessor-qualified MsgApp. Followers check predecessor and committed-prefix conflicts, append only conflicting suffixes, bound advertised commit, and queue replies. Both follower replies and leader self-acks pass through msgsAfterAppend; legal publication relies on caller persistence, directly via Ready/Advance or ordered async append Responses. The leader term-filters replies and raises sender Match. Tracker considers only active voters, majority order statistics and both halves of joint configuration. raftLog.maybeCommit additionally requires the candidate entry to match the current term. Commit propagates via append or Match-capped heartbeat. Ready exports committed entries; async apply waits for local stability. Application and public client completion remain separate caller actions; proposal acceptance does not promise commitment.

context.explanation: Ticks or Campaign trigger hup only when promotable and without unapplied committed configuration changes. PreVote can gather prospective support without increasing term; real candidacy resets state, increments term and records self vote. Self and remote vote replies are queued behind persistence. Vote grants require vote/leader eligibility and last-log freshness. Matching response type and active voter quorum determine victory; the new leader resets progress and appends its current-term empty entry. Higher-term messages normally force follower transition, with lease/pre-vote exceptions; obsolete responses are rejected. CheckQuorum can cause same-term stepdown. Transfer pauses proposals, catches the target up and sends TimeoutNow; timeout or ineligibility aborts transfer. Restart restores HardState/log/configuration and starts as follower. Configuration entries activate through ApplyConfChange, changing voters and optionally causing removal stepdown.

connection.explanation: Term/role reset clears election tally, remote replication support and readOnly acknowledgments, while preserving log and committed prefix; current-term matching prevents a fresh leader from advancing commitment solely using an old-term candidate index. Queued/in-flight responses may outlive resets, so Step term checks remain necessary. StorageAppendResp carries both creation term and entry identity: old-term entry stabilization is skipped even if entry term/index recur, but committed snapshot application survives that term change. StorageApplyResp is term-zero and represents committed work independent of leadership. Configuration changes retain existing participant progress but change which IDs count; switching configuration can immediately rerun commitment. Snapshots recover configuration as well as log boundary. Safe reads wait for current-term commitment (except singleton shortcut), track context-specific heartbeat acknowledgments under active voters, then expose read index to a caller that still must wait for application. reset replaces readOnly but does not clear pendingReadIndexMessages; release retries them only after a current-term commit, creating fresh acknowledgment tracking.

grounding.derivation: ReadOnlySafe guarantees reads through quorum communication; Node/RawNode describe the returned request-specific index as a safe application barrier. A sole voter can supply local quorum authority only if it is the serving node. Config changes take effect when applied, and StepDownOnRemoval makes role demotion optional without declaring that unsafe read results are permitted. Therefore a removed node with no fresh sole-voter support cannot use only local state as safe authority. This requirement allows silence/forwarding/rejection and does not infer liveness or demand a stale client result.
grounding.applicability: At the RawNode library boundary, ReadIndex has no stated membership precondition or automatic Stop, and ApplyConfChange documentation requires applying the removal rather than forbidding later API calls. External routing that stops removed nodes is a deployment mitigation outside this scope. The check uses actual committed removal, callbacks, elections and ordered storage; it does not arbitrarily install a config.

alternatives: Enabling StepDownOnRemoval is an existing protection and will be measured as a no-output control.
